This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   The overarching task is running the **zimmerMANNBuild** skill (a Zimmermann PWA Kit-specific closed-loop build workflow: Implementer → Tester → Orchestrator → Scorer → visual checkpoint → commit, repeated per planned step) to implement **SFCC-236 "Product Card Shared Component"** — a shared, variation-driven product card (`plp`/`home`/`wishlist`) for the Zimmermann PWA Kit, per a 7-step plan produced earlier by `zimmerMANNPreBuild`/`zm-planner`. SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 (Recently Viewed stories) were explicitly held out of scope per the user's earlier decision.

   Explicit, verbatim-important user directives issued during this build (all currently binding):
   - "hey claude, ready to work?" — session start.
   - "let's make sure that all our local active branches are up to date, and make sure we have all branches in the github remote repo locally available" (pre-build housekeeping, completed earlier).
   - `/zimmerMANNPreBuild` invocation with 3 Jira links (SFCC-236, SFCC-83, "SFC-84" typo resolved to SFCC-84) — "it's hammertime - maximum effort, let's build."
   - Multiple AskUserQuestion resolutions during planning (arrows-vs-indicator = "position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"; touch paging = "scroll-snap it is"; naming collision = "ZimmSizeChip (recommended)"; badge = "no design exists needing a badge in the image, take this out").
   - "verify the claim one consumer only for linkSm" — demanding independent re-verification rather than trusting a prior claim.
   - **"let's make sure to run in-depth visual checks against the design during our looping"** — standing directive.
   - **"nothing is to be 'assumed', everything must trace back to an actual design spec"** — standing directive, explicitly invoked again for Step 6: "run it, let's make sure to implement the 'no assumptions, everything up to design spec' and 'full visual checks'."
   - "have we done the full visual check for this commit?" — a direct challenge that led to discovering 2 more real bugs in Step 5 after I had prematurely reported it as fully checked.
   - "check the remaining two, then commit" — Loading Price story + Mobile Figma cross-check, both completed, one (mobile padding) revealing a real gap that was fixed.
   - "clean the stray change" (twice, for two different stray uncommitted Storybook writebacks on story files not related to the current step).
   - Step-completion approvals: "LGTM - let's move forward" (Step 1), "LGTM, off to the next" (Step 2), "cool ... let's make sure to implement..." (Step 6 kickoff), "run it" (Step 6).
   - Commit approvals given only after explicit "commit"/"go next"/"LGTM ... commit" instructions per each step — no step has been committed without an explicit go-ahead.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Zimmermann PWA Kit override architecture**: `overrides/app/` shadows `@salesforce/retail-react-app`; TypeScript-only; Chakra UI theming via `useMultiStyleConfig`/co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipes; `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties as the only sanctioned way to reference design tokens in JSX (never bare Chakra token keys); `textStyle` prop mandatory for all typography.
   - **ui-kits atomic structure**: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/` with a mandatory four-file pattern (`index.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `<name>.css.ts`), tier determined by composition depth not folder.
   - **Recipe governance tests**: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` (declared `parts` array must exactly match `styles.X` reads) and `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (hard gate: no bare Chakra token keys, no accidental base-SFCC-recipe-name collision) — both run on every `npm run test` and were repeatedly the mechanism that caught/prevented regressions.
   - **`.zimm-*` global class registry vs `textStyle`**: `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` composes `.zimm-*` classes from `zimmTokens.ts`; per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, `.zimm-*` classes are reserved for genuinely static non-interactive treatments — anything with interactive state (`_hover`/`_focusVisible`) must use `textStyle`/Chakra recipes instead, because a class "mirror" is structurally incomplete and can silently drift from the real theme config (this happened for real with `linkSm`).
   - **Tier 1/Tier 2 approval protocol**: `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` (Tier 1) / `protectedFiles.md` (Tier 2); AGENTS.md's "Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced" section — verified via `gh api user --jq .login` then `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'`; confirmed `marcelannavarro` is a member (alongside `hanl`, `TimLavelleACC`), permitting direct edits to Tier 1 files (e.g. `theme/foundation/typography.ts`) with the file named and reasoning stated, no separate confirmation gate needed — but Hard Rule #10 (never cross more than one tier without confirming scope) was still explicitly honored via an AskUserQuestion before touching the second (Tier 2) file.
   - **Discriminated union + VARIATION_CONFIG pattern**: `ZimmProductCardProps = BaseProps & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)`, with a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG` object (not a function, not a switch) driving every visibility/behavior decision — the render body must contain zero `switch`/`if` on `props.variation`. Proven via `@ts-expect-error` compile-time tests.
   - **Stretched-link pattern**: exactly one real `<a>` per card (in `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `nameLink`, built via `chakra(RouteLink)` from `react-router-dom`); the organism's own recipe adds `[data-card-slot="content"] a::after {content:'', position:'absolute', inset:0}` to stretch it over the whole card; every OTHER interactive control gets `position:relative; zIndex:1` to lift above the invisible overlay. Requires the containing-block chain (from the `<a>` up to the organism's `position:relative` root) to have no intermediate `position:relative` ancestors.
   - **`data-card-slot` cross-component selector contract**: stable attribute values (`media`, `close`, `carousel`, `indicator` from Media; `content`, `price`, `sizeChips` from Content) that the organism's own recipe targets via descendant selectors for hover-reveal CSS, without either molecule needing to know about the organism.
   - **`(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` media query**: the established mechanism (from Step 4) for splitting desktop-hover-only affordances (arrows, price/size-chip reveal) from touch-only affordances (slide indicator), used consistently through Steps 4-6.
   - **`:focus-within` / `_focusWithin` keyboard-equivalence pattern**: established precedent in `zimmSearchInput.css.ts`/`globalStyles.ts`; added in Step 6 alongside every `:hover` reveal rule so keyboard-only Tab users can also reveal hover-gated content — critical WCAG 2.1.1 compliance mechanism used repeatedly (Step 4's scroll-container keyboard fix, Step 6's size-chip reveal fix).
   - **jsdom limitations discovered/proven this session**: (a) jsdom does zero layout/paint/hit-testing, so interaction tests (`fireEvent.click`) dispatch directly to a named node regardless of what real CSS stacking-order would resolve — proven by deliberately breaking z-index and observing zero test failures; (b) in this project's jsdom, `window.getComputedStyle()` does NOT dynamically re-resolve Emotion-injected pseudo-class-gated rules after a real `.focus()` call, even though `document.activeElement`/`element.matches(':focus-within')` correctly update — worked around using `.matches()` instead of `getComputedStyle()`.
   - **MemoryRouter**: Storybook wraps stories in a `MemoryRouter` (React Router), which manages navigation state entirely in memory and never touches `window.location.href` — the correct signal for detecting real-browser navigation in this environment is `document.activeElement` (confirming the correct `<a href>` received focus/click), not `location.href`.
   - **Browser-pane coordinate systems**: the `computer` tool's screenshot-pixel coordinate space does NOT match raw `getBoundingClientRect()` values read via `javascript_tool` (different scale factors) — mixing them produces nonsensical results (discovered via a genuine methodology mistake mid-session); the reliable method is always: screenshot first, identify the target visually in that exact screenshot's own pixel space, click at that same coordinate.
   - **Figma tools used extensively**: `mcp__plugin_figma_figma__get_metadata` (structural tree + `hidden` attributes — the most reliable ground truth), `get_screenshot` (visual reference, downloaded via `curl` and read via the `Read` tool), `get_design_context` (generates React+Tailwind approximation code with real computed CSS values/tokens — useful for exact spacing/colour/copy but NOT reliable for exact vertical-alignment arithmetic, which needed live-DOM verification instead).
   - **Real falsification-based testing discipline** (mandated throughout this build): every claimed test/fix must be proven by deliberately breaking the thing it protects, confirming the test fails, then reverting and confirming it passes — "a check must be made to fail on purpose once before its pass counts" (per user's own `feedback_prove_dont_assert` memory principle, though not explicitly re-cited this session, it was the operative discipline).

3. Files and Code Sections:

   **Planning artifacts** (outside the repo, per skill rules — `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/`):
   - `findings.md` — the 29-row PreBuild gate table, iteratively updated with Figma resolution results, badge/notify-me corrections, etc.
   - `plan.md` — the 7-step build plan, iteratively updated with §4a (arrows/indicator), §4b (scroll-snap), §4c (badge investigation, later superseded), §4d (naming collision resolution), §4e (badge removal, supersedes §4c).

   **Committed files** (all on branch `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, cut from `origin/develop`):

   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts}` — commit `0cee6c9`. Touch-only position readout, composes into Media in Step 4. Recipe key `ZimmSlideIndicator`, parts `['root','dot']`. Fixed: wrong token category (`--zimm-color-text-default`→`--zimm-color-bg-05`), wrong Storybook category (`Elements/`→`Commerce/`), uncitable "plan §4a" comments removed.

   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSizeChip/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSizeChip.css.ts,zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts}` + `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts}` — commit `b42d17a`. Renamed from `ZimmSizeSelector`/`ZimmSizeSelectorOption` due to collision with unrelated branch `feature/SFCC-92_pdp-size-selection-add-to-bag`. Key exported resolvers: `resolveBorderColour`, `resolveBackgroundColour`, `resolveTextColour` (exported specifically to enable `zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts` coverage after Tester proved they were untested). Final corrected visual states (verified against real Figma PNG exports of nodes `40003038:125873/125874/125875/130506`): Default = no border, Disabled = no border + muted text, Selected = border-only (`--zimm-color-border-focus`) + normal text (NOT filled/inverted), Focus = border + outline ring.

   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx}` — commit `e66451e`. Added `isLive?: boolean` (default `true`) opt-out for `aria-live`/`aria-atomic`, needed because a PLP grid of many cards shouldn't carry 60 live regions. Additive-only change; default path proven byte-identical via 3 independent falsification mutations.

   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts}` — commit `c3eff5c`. Image gallery: scroll-snap, `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'` gating arrows-vs-indicator (never both), always-on keyboard operability via `canNavigateByKeyboard`/`handleScrollContainerKeyDown` (WCAG 2.1.1 fix), `close` overlay (wishlist remove, top-right, 48×48), NO badge/tag slot (removed per user's explicit "take this out" instruction — originally had a `tag` part/prop, fully deleted: `badge` prop, `TAG_MIN_WIDTH` constant, `WithBadge` story, related tests). Fixed a serious layout bug: Storybook decorator `<Box maxWidth="320px">` → `<Box width="320px">` (the component's fully-percentage-based sizing chain had no definite-size anchor, causing every single-image story to render at 8×12px instead of a full card).

   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmProductCardContent.css.ts}` + `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` + `overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts` + `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` — commit `f775026`. Text block: name link (`chakra(RouteLink)`), bag button (`Icon_bag`, confirmed not a wishlist star), attributes row (wishlist-only colour+size, rendered as `` `${colour},` `` + `size` with `gap: var(--zimm-scale-3xs)` = 2px, NOT the originally-shipped 4px), price (always `isLive={false}`), size-chip slot (rendered unconditionally when `showSizeChips`, NOT hidden by this component's own recipe — hover-reveal is the organism's job), notify-me link (real Figma copy "Notify me" with `textStyle:'linkSm'` and `color: var(--zimm-color-link-default)`, NOT `text-default`). `root` part gained responsive padding: mobile `paddingTop: var(--zimm-scale-m)` (16px) / `paddingInline: var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` (32px), desktop (`@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.md})`) `paddingTop: var(--zimm-scale-2xl)` (32px) / `paddingInline: var(--zimm-scale-3xl)` (40px) — imported `breakpoints` from `app/theme/foundation`, following `footerShared.ts`'s established precedent (media queries can't consume `var()`). Also fixed the systemic `linkSm.textTransform`: `capitalize`→`uppercase` in BOTH `theme/foundation/typography.ts` (Tier 1) and `theme/globalStyles.ts`'s `zimmTextLinkSm` (Tier 2) — the second was found only after the user demanded re-verification ("verify the claim one consumer only for linkSm"), and was an ACTIVELY FAILING test (`theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard) before the fix.

   **Currently uncommitted (Step 6, in progress)**:
   - `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmProductCard.css.ts}` (untracked, new) + `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (modified, +2 lines: import + registration).
   - Key exported types: `ZimmProductCardBaseProps`, `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation`, `ZimmProductCardHomeVariation`, `ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation`, `ZimmProductCardProps` (all exported — forced by TS excess-property-checking being weak against unions, proven via `@ts-expect-error` tests).
   - `VARIATION_CONFIG` — confirmed-correct matrix (verified cell-by-cell by both Tester and Orchestrator against real Figma `hidden` attributes):
     ```
     Home:     showBag=false, showAttributes=false, showSizeChips=false, hoverRevealsPrice=true,  hoverHidesPrice=false, hoverRevealsSizeSelector=false
     PLP:      showBag=true,  showAttributes=false, showSizeChips=true,  hoverHidesPrice=true,    hoverRevealsPrice=false, hoverRevealsSizeSelector=true
     Wishlist: showBag=true,  showAttributes=true,  showSizeChips=true,  hoverHidesPrice=true,    hoverRevealsPrice=false, hoverRevealsSizeSelector=true, showRemove=true
     ```
   - **Confirmed real bug (found by Tester, FIXED in round 1)**: `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s lift rule `'[data-card-slot="close"]': {position:'relative', zIndex:1}` had higher CSS specificity than Media's own `position:'absolute'` on that element, breaking the wishlist remove button's pinned top-right position (fell into normal document flow). Fixed by removing the competing `position:'relative'`, keeping only `zIndex:1` (element already positioned by Media's own recipe). The other two lift rules (`[data-card-slot="carousel"] button`, `[data-card-slot="content"] button`) were correctly left with `position:'relative'` since those targets have no prior `position` set.
   - **Confirmed UNDER-scope (found by Orchestrator, FIXED in round 1)**: size-chip reveal was gated only on `&:hover` with no `:focus-within` equivalent, making it unreachable by keyboard (an explicit, stated Step 6 pass criterion). Fixed by adding `:focus-within` sibling keys alongside every `:hover` reveal rule (price-hide, price-reveal, size-chip-reveal), matching `zimmSearchInput.css.ts`/`globalStyles.ts`'s established idiom.
   - **Confirmed gap, correctly DEFERRED (Fix 3, not shipped)**: Mobile PLP/PDP Default (Figma `40002163:41477`/`40002163:41479`) has the bag icon `hidden="true"`; Desktop always shows it. `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBag` has no mobile/desktop split. The Implementer evaluated and rejected two candidate CSS selectors (a nesting-depth selector would also hide size chips — proven identical DOM depth; an `aria-label`-presence selector relies on an undocumented coincidence of Content's current implementation). Correctly identified this needs a new `data-card-slot="bag"` attribute added to the ALREADY-COMMITTED `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` (Step 5) — out of Step 6's file scope, requires explicit sign-off before touching committed work. **This decision point has been surfaced to the user but not yet formally decided.**
   - Also noted: `showNotifyMe` is computed uniformly across all three variations (`Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe)`), not restricted to `plp` — reviewed by both Tester and Orchestrator, judged as within-scope/forward-compatible (Content's own contract already delegates this resolution to the organism), not blocking, but flagged as worth a second look before SFCC-90/497 build real callers.
   - No `priority` (LCP escape hatch) passthrough to Media — honestly documented as a "KNOWN GAP" in the organism's own docblock, not silently dropped.

4. Errors and fixes:

   - **Naming collision (Step 2)**: Plan originally named components `ZimmSizeSelectorOption`/`ZimmSizeSelector`, discovered via `git log` to collide with unrelated, unmerged, same-day work on `feature/SFCC-92_pdp-size-selection-add-to-bag` (a completely different dropdown-based PDP component). Fixed by renaming to `ZimmSizeChip`/`ZimmSizeChipGroup` after user's explicit AskUserQuestion choice.

   - **Step 2 visual fidelity bug**: Automated loop passed all axes, but I personally caught (via real Figma PNG downloads) that the shipped chip states were structurally backwards from the design (bordered-by-default should be borderless-by-default; filled-when-selected should be outline-only-when-selected). Fixed via targeted dispatch, re-verified via live `getComputedStyle`.

   - **Step 4 layout collapse bug**: All jsdom tests green, but every single-image Storybook story rendered at 8×12px. Root-caused precisely to `<Box maxWidth="320px">` (should be `width="320px"`) in the decorator, combined with the component's fully-percentage-relative sizing chain having no definite-size anchor. Verified the fix hypothesis live (via injected `element.style.width` before dispatching a fix), then dispatched and re-verified in Storybook.

   - **Step 5 notify-me fabrication**: Built from an unconfirmed plan default ("Notify me when back in stock") rather than a real design. User caught this ("nothing like this in the designs"). Real Figma copy is "Notify me" (styled uppercase via CSS, not authored as literal caps — to preserve i18n correctness).

   - **Step 5 `linkSm` self-report discrepancy**: An earlier Implementer dispatch was told NOT to touch `theme/foundation/typography.ts` (Tier 1) and to instead leave a "FINDING" comment — but its actual on-disk edit (discovered via file mtime + diff) shows it DID make the edit and its own report claimed it hadn't. Flagged transparently to the user as a real "agent said X, did Y" issue.

   - **Step 5 incomplete `linkSm` fix**: When the user demanded "verify the claim one consumer only," a broader unrestricted grep (not excluding stories/tests) revealed a second, parallel `.zimm-text-link-sm` definition in `globalStyles.ts` that had NOT been updated and was causing `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard test to ACTIVELY FAIL. Fixed with explicit user approval for the second (Tier 2) file, per Hard Rule #10.

   - **Step 5 attributes-row bugs**: found via a proper Figma-vs-Storybook comparison prompted by "have we done the full visual check for this commit?" — gap was 4px (should be 2px, real token `--zimm-scale-3xs` existed unused) and colour+size text had no comma (should render "Ivory, M" as one continuous phrase, per Figma's actual text-node structure with the comma baked into the colour node). Fixed with real ink-to-ink glyph measurement (canvas TextMetrics) proving the CSS-gap-only approach visually reads correctly without needing a literal space character.

   - **Step 5 missing responsive padding**: found via the user's "check the remaining two" instruction (Mobile Figma cross-check). `root` had NO padding at all on ANY breakpoint — not just an unhandled mobile case. Fixed using the `footerShared.ts`-established pattern of importing the real `breakpoints` token (media queries can't consume `var()`).

   - **Step 6 close-button z-index bug**: Tester found via literal `getComputedStyle` on a real (unmocked) render that the organism's lift rule's competing `position:'relative'` won the CSS specificity battle against Media's own `position:'absolute'`, breaking the wishlist remove button's positioning. Fixed by removing the redundant `position` value.

   - **Step 6 keyboard-inaccessible size chips**: Orchestrator found the size-chip hover-reveal had no `:focus-within` equivalent (an explicit, stated pass criterion, not a newly-discovered gap). Fixed by mirroring the established `_focusWithin` idiom.

   - **My own browser-automation methodology errors during the Step 6 real-browser check** (most recent, in-progress work):
     - Mixed `computer` tool's screenshot-pixel coordinates with raw `getBoundingClientRect()` JS values (different scale factors: screenshot 800px wide vs. JS-reported frameRect 980px wide) — produced a nonsensical negative `iframeX` and a false "click landed on nothing" (`elementFromPoint` returned null). **Fix**: abandoned raw-coordinate cross-referencing; reverted to the reliable method of screenshotting first, visually identifying the target in that exact screenshot's pixel space, then clicking there.
     - Checked `window.location.href` to detect navigation, which never changes because Storybook wraps stories in a `MemoryRouter` (deliberately keeps routing state in memory only). **Fix**: switched to checking `document.activeElement` (tag, `href` attribute, `textContent`) as the correct signal.
     - Got a false "hover didn't revert" result twice at two different "mouse away" coordinates — investigated and correctly diagnosed as `:focus-within` (Fix 2) correctly keeping the reveal state active because the `<a>` element was still focused from an earlier click-through test, NOT a stuck `:hover` bug. Confirmed by checking `document.activeElement` before an explicit `.blur()` call, then re-checking computed styles reverted correctly after blur.
     - Clicked at a visually-estimated coordinate (383, 185) for the "Next image" arrow button on the PLP/Multiple-Images story and missed (confirmed via `document.activeElement` showing the link was activated instead of the arrow button) — was in the process of correcting this via `scrollIntoView({block:'center', inline:'center'})` + a fresh screenshot when the summary request interrupted the work.

5. Problem Solving:

   Solved: naming collision resolution (Step 2), 8 real Figma-vs-build discrepancies caught via active verification rather than trusting green automated tests (Step 2 chip states; Step 4 layout collapse + badge removal; Step 5 notify-me copy/colour/spacing, name/bag alignment, `linkSm` drift across two files, attributes gap+comma, missing responsive padding; Step 6 close-button z-index bug), one genuine self-report discrepancy from a prior agent dispatch (flagged transparently), and — in the most recent work — three real-browser interaction mechanics for Step 6 fully confirmed working (close button pinned + clickable, bag button clickable, and critically the stretched-link overlay genuinely navigates when clicking anywhere on the product image, plus hover-reveal and focus-within-reveal-and-revert both confirmed via live CSS state).

   Ongoing/unresolved:
   - The PLP "Multiple Images" story's arrow-button click test is mid-correction (scrolled into view, screenshot not yet retaken, click not yet retried with corrected coordinates).
   - Fix 3 (mobile PLP bag-icon visibility) remains an open, deferred decision requiring the user's explicit sign-off on touching the already-committed `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` to add a `data-card-slot="bag"` attribute — not yet formally decided.
   - Step 6 has not yet been committed (still verifying via real browser before committing, per the standing "full visual checks" directive and the Scorer's own explicit note that round-2 PASS does not substitute for this check).
   - Step 7 (final gate: `tsc`/`lint`/`test`/`audit:tokens`/CodeRabbit review + PR handoff to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`) has not started.

content.text: Found a real bug — the desktop arrow buttons are unclickable because the stretched card-link overlay paints on top of them. Let me confirm the root cause in the organism's recipe file before fixing it.

content.content:
1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
5	 * arrows/indicator split — repeated here as this file's own module-private copy (not shared via
6	 * an import) matching that file's own precedent of not exporting/sharing the literal. Governs
7	 * the price <-> size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage
8	 * together off the exact same media feature, on this shared root.
9	 */
10	const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';
11	
12	type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
13	  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
14	   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
15	  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
16	  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
17	   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
18	  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
19	  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
20	   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
21	   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
22	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
23	};
24	
25	/**
26	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
27	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
28	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
29	 * own by itself:
30	 *
31	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
32	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
33	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
34	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
35	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
36	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
37	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
38	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
39	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
40	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
41	 *      Three separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
42	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
43	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
44	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but three plain keys need no such
45	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
46	 *      TWO of the three (`carousel`/`content` buttons) also add `position: relative` — those
47	 *      elements are `position: static` by default in their own component recipes, so a positioned
48	 *      ancestor is needed for z-index to apply at all. The `close` button is the one exception:
49	 *      `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `close` recipe part already sets `position: absolute` on it
50	 *      directly, so it needs (and, as of the Fix 1 rework below, gets) only the z-index bump here
51	 *      — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER specificity
52	 *      than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector; Media's is a
53	 *      single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out of its pinned
54	 *      top-right corner into normal document flow. See the inline comment at that key below and
55	 *      index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe blocks for the proof.
56	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
57	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
58	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
59	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:focus-within` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below) — `:hover`
60	 *      alone would leave every reveal permanently unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable
61	 *      device, since `display: none` removes the unconditional-state element from the tab order
62	 *      entirely and nothing but a real pointer hover could ever have revealed it.
63	 *
64	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
65	 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
66	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
67	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
68	 *
69	 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
70	 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
71	 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
72	 * the three lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
73	 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
74	 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
75	 */
76	export const ZimmProductCard = {
77	  parts: ['root'],
78	
79	  baseStyle: ({
80	    hoverHidesPrice,
81	    hoverRevealsPrice,
82	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
83	  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
84	    root: {
85	      position: 'relative',
86	      width: '100%',
87	
88	      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
89	      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
90	      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
91	      '[data-card-slot="content"] a::after': {
92	        content: '""',
93	        position: 'absolute',
94	        inset: 0,
95	      },
96	
97	      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
98	      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
99	      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
100	      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
101	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
102	      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own
103	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
104	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
105	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
106	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
107	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
108	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
109	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
110	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
111	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
112	      '[data-card-slot="close"]': {
113	        zIndex: 1,
114	      },
115	      '[data-card-slot="carousel"] button': {
116	        position: 'relative',
117	        zIndex: 1,
118	      },
119	      '[data-card-slot="content"] button': {
120	        position: 'relative',
121	        zIndex: 1,
122	      },
123	
124	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
125	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
126	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
127	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
128	      ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
129	        // Home: price starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
130	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
131	      }),
132	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
133	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
134	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'none' },
135	      }),
136	
137	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {

432	Creates `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, the union, `VARIATION_CONFIG`, the composition, the stretched link, and
433	`zimmProductCard.css.ts` holding **all** hover-reveal rules.
434	
435	- Union enforced at compile time: `variation:'wishlist'` without `onRemove`/`colour`/`size` fails `tsc`;
436	  `variation:'home'` given `onRemove` fails `tsc`. Two `@ts-expect-error` cases — these are the extensibility
437	  AC's real proof.
438	- **Extensibility:** `index.tsx` contains no `switch`/`if` on `props.variation`; every layout decision reads
439	  from the config object.
440	- **AC1 across all variations:** six cases (plp/home/wishlist × unavailable true/false) assert the primary image.
441	- **Exactly one `<a>` per card** — `getAllByRole('link')` length 1. Every control separately focusable.
442	- Keyboard equivalence: with `:focus-within`, size options and arrows are Tab-reachable in jsdom.
443	- **Hover rules asserted structurally:** import the recipe object and assert (a) the root part has a
444	  `:hover, :focus-within` key, (b) nested inside `@media (min-width: ...) and (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`,
445	  (c) the selector targets the imported `data-card-slot` constants, not a string literal.
446	  **Each assertion must be made to fail on purpose once before being accepted.**
447	- Below `CARD_BP.desktop` no rule reveals the size selector — matching the mobile AC.
448	- Recipe key is `ZimmProductCard`, not `ProductCard` (`recipeGuards.test.ts:357`).
449	- All six recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
450	- Story `Commerce/ZimmProductCard`: `Default` (mandatory), `PLP`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Home`, `Wishlist`,
451	  `SingleImage`, `WithBadge`. No `play` asserting hover — CSS media queries don't evaluate there; each
452	  hover-dependent story carries a docs note for manual review.

### Step 6 — `ZimmProductCard` organism + variation config + shared module
Creates `zimmProductCardShared.ts`, the union, `VARIATION_CONFIG`, the composition, the stretched link, and
`zimmProductCard.css.ts` holding **all** hover-reveal rules.

- Union enforced at compile time: `variation:'wishlist'` without `onRemove`/`colour`/`size` fails `tsc`;
  `variation:'home'` given `onRemove` fails `tsc`. Two `@ts-expect-error` cases — these are the extensibility
  AC's real proof.
- **Extensibility:** `index.tsx` contains no `switch`/`if` on `props.variation`; every layout decision reads
  from the config object.
- **AC1 across all variations:** six cases (plp/home/wishlist × unavailable true/false) assert the primary image.
- **Exactly one `<a>` per card** — `getAllByRole('link')` length 1. Every control separately focusable.
- Keyboard equivalence: with `:focus-within`, size options and arrows are Tab-reachable in jsdom.
- **Hover rules asserted structurally:** import the recipe object and assert (a) the root part has a
  `:hover, :focus-within` key, (b) nested inside `@media (min-width: ...) and (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`,
  (c) the selector targets the imported `data-card-slot` constants, not a string literal.
  **Each assertion must be made to fail on purpose once before being accepted.**
- Below `CARD_BP.desktop` no rule reveals the size selector — matching the mobile AC.
- Recipe key is `ZimmProductCard`, not `ProductCard` (`recipeGuards.test.ts:357`).
- All six recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
- Story `Commerce/ZimmProductCard`: `Default` (mandatory), `PLP`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Home`, `Wishlist`,
  `SingleImage`, `WithBadge`. No `play` asserting hover — CSS media queries don't evaluate there; each
  hover-dependent story carries a docs note for manual review.
- Organism function stays under ~150 lines.
- `ZimmProductCardProps` and the three member types **are exported** (deviating from the exemplar) because they
  are the contract SFCC-80/90/497 will type their mappers against. Document the deviation in JSDoc.

### Step 7 — Gate and PR
`tsc --noEmit` · `lint` · `test` · `audit:tokens` · `coderabbit auth status` then `cr review --light --base develop`.

- All clean, or every `audit:tokens` finding traced to a pre-existing violation outside this diff.

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Recipe for the PDP size-chip group. Two mutually-exclusive root renders, matching the two
5	 * "Type" variants of the size-chip Figma component set (node 40003066:34868):
6	 *   - `radiogroup` — the multi-size row (the default Type, 208x28 in Figma) — lays out
7	 *     ZimmSizeChip atoms in a row; each chip's own fill/border/focus styling stays in the
8	 *     sibling ZimmSizeChip atom's own recipe, this part is layout only.
9	 *   - `oneSize` — the single non-interactive label shown when only one size is offered (the
10	 *     other Type, 65x28 in Figma) — a genuinely different, non-interactive component, not a
11	 *     radiogroup with one item.
12	 */
13	export const ZimmSizeChipGroup = {
14	  parts: ['radiogroup', 'oneSize'],
15	  baseStyle: (): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
16	    radiogroup: {
17	      display: 'flex',
18	      alignItems: 'center',
19	      // No inter-chip gap value confirmed for this exact node — left at the flex default (no
20	      // `gap` declared) rather than invented, same precedent as
21	      // zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts's `pagination` part.
22	    },
23	
24	    oneSize: {
25	      display: 'flex',
26	      alignItems: 'center',
27	      justifyContent: 'center',
28	      // The non-interactive single-label footprint from the size-chip Figma component set's
29	      // other Type — no matching width-scale token for 65px; height reuses the same
30	      // --zimm-scale-700 (28px) the ZimmSizeChip atom's own `chip` part uses, since it is the
31	      // same row height as the interactive variant.
32	      // audit-allow: 65px — no foundation width token exists for this exact non-interactive
33	      // label size
34	      width: '65px',
35	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)',
36	      textStyle: 'buttonSm',
37	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
38	    },
39	  }),
40	};

content.text:
I finished the visual audit against real Figma states. There are two small fixes and one more substantial, systemic gap — here's what I found, all confirmed against the live Figma component set (`40000223:2822`), not assumed:

**Finding A — size chips render with zero gap (Step 2 file, already committed)**
`zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts`'s `radiogroup` part deliberately shipped with no `justifyContent`/`gap` ("no inter-chip gap value confirmed"). Figma's real `SizeSelector` node uses `justify-content: space-between` across the full card-content width. Confirmed live: chips currently sit pixel-flush against each other (28px apart, 28px wide = 0 gap).

**Finding B — Wishlist story never demonstrates its own hover state**
Unlike `Default`/`PLP`, the `Wishlist` story never passes `sizeChipValues`/`onSizeChipSelect`, so hovering it today just shows an empty gap where chips should be. Not a component bug — Content correctly renders an empty wrapper — but it means the story never actually shows Wishlist's real hover behavior.

**Finding C — unavailable items shouldn't get the size-selector swap, and "Notify me" should be hover-gated, not always-on**
Checked Default+Hover for all three variations × unavailable, including Mobile (no-hover) unavailable. The consistent rule across every one:
- When `isUnavailable`, hover must **not** swap price→size-chips (nothing to pick) — price stays visible throughout (confirmed identically for PLP and Wishlist).
- "Notify me" is **hover-revealed on hover-capable devices** (hidden by default, shown on hover/focus-within) but **always visible on touch** (confirmed via the Mobile unavailable variants, which have no hover state at all).

Today's code does neither: `VARIATION_CONFIG`'s hover flags ignore `isUnavailable` entirely (so PLP/Wishlist still swap to size-chips even out of stock), and `showNotifyMe` renders the button unconditionally whenever mounted — no hover-gating, and it currently has no `data-card-slot` for CSS to target at all.

Fixing C touches three files: `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` and `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (both Step 6, uncommitted) plus adding one `data-card-slot="notifyMe"` attribute to the already-committed `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx` (Step 5).

1	import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	/**
4	 * Same hover-capable-pointer gate `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already establishes for its own
5	 * arrows/indicator split — repeated here as this file's own module-private copy (not shared via
6	 * an import) matching that file's own precedent of not exporting/sharing the literal. Governs
7	 * the price <-> size-selector swap below, so both composed children's hover treatments engage
8	 * together off the exact same media feature, on this shared root.
9	 */
10	const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';
11	
12	type ZimmProductCardStyleProps = {
13	  /** Home only — see VARIATION_CONFIG in index.tsx. Price is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer
14	   *  type by default and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card. */
15	  hoverRevealsPrice?: boolean;
16	  /** PLP + Wishlist — price is visible by default (Content's own natural rendering; no override
17	   *  needed for that half) and hides only once a hover-capable pointer hovers the card. */
18	  hoverHidesPrice?: boolean;
19	  /** PLP + Wishlist — the size-chip picker is hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type by default
20	   *  and only appears once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card, in the same
21	   *  media-query gate as the price swap above so both engage together. */
22	  hoverRevealsSizeSelector?: boolean;
23	};
24	
25	/**
26	 * Recipe for the product-card organism (ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard) — composes
27	 * ZimmProductCardMedia (Step 4) and ZimmProductCardContent (Step 5) with no styling of its own
28	 * for either child. This recipe's entire job is the cross-component concerns neither child can
29	 * own by itself:
30	 *
31	 *   1. THE STRETCHED-LINK OVERLAY. ZimmProductCardContent's `nameLink` renders the one real `<a>`
32	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
33	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
34	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
35	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
36	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
37	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,
38	 *      never an ancestor of Content's `<a>`, so it has no bearing on this chain.)
39	 *   2. LIFTING EVERY OTHER INTERACTIVE CONTROL above that overlay — a z-index higher than the
40	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
41	 *      Three separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
42	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
43	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
44	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but three plain keys need no such
45	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
46	 *      ONE of the three (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
47	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
48	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close` and `carousel` are the two exceptions:
49	 *      `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly (`close` via
50	 *      `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute, top: 50%, ...`),
51	 *      so each needs (and gets) only the z-index bump here:
52	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
53	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
54	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
55	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
56	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
57	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the
58	 *          round-2 Scorer PASS, which explicitly flagged that check as still outstanding, not by
59	 *          any automated pass). The lift rule used to target
60	 *          `'[data-card-slot="carousel"] button'` — the two arrow BUTTONS individually, each given
61	 *          its own `position: relative, zIndex: 1` — identical in shape to the `content button`
62	 *          rule above, and every jsdom test passed. A real click in a real browser still landed on
63	 *          the overlay, not the arrow. Root cause: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `carousel` part
64	 *          sets `transform: translateY(-50%)` (to vertically centre the arrow row against `slide`),
65	 *          and `transform` unconditionally creates a NEW stacking context on that element,
66	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
67	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles
68	 *          against the *other* arrow button, never against anything outside `carousel` (like the
69	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
70	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
71	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
72	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
73	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
74	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
75	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
76	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
77	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
78	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.
79	 *   3. THE HOVER-REVEAL SWAP between price and the PLP/Wishlist size-selector (and Home's
80	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
81	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
82	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:focus-within` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below) — `:hover`
83	 *      alone would leave every reveal permanently unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable
84	 *      device, since `display: none` removes the unconditional-state element from the tab order
85	 *      entirely and nothing but a real pointer hover could ever have revealed it.
86	 *
87	 * Parts: only `root` is declared. Everything above is a nested descendant selector inside
88	 * `root`'s own style object (targeting the composed children's `data-card-slot` attributes), not
89	 * a separate Chakra part — `index.tsx` never reads anything off `useMultiStyleConfig` but
90	 * `styles.root`, so `recipeParts.test.ts`'s declared-vs-read reconciliation needs nothing more.
91	 *
92	 * `zIndex: 1` below is this file's one deliberately unnamed magic number — accepted per
93	 * .claude/rules/conventions.md's own exception ("0, 1, -1 in obvious idiomatic uses"): it is the
94	 * standard "one level above the default/auto stacking layer" value, used identically at each of
95	 * the three lift points, and the stretched-link overlay is deliberately left with no z-index of
96	 * its own rather than pinned to a specific lower number — so the two sides only ever need to be
97	 * *some* value vs a *higher* one, never a specific pair.
98	 */
99	export const ZimmProductCard = {
100	  parts: ['root'],
101	
102	  baseStyle: ({
103	    hoverHidesPrice,
104	    hoverRevealsPrice,
105	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
106	  }: ZimmProductCardStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
107	    root: {
108	      position: 'relative',
109	      width: '100%',
110	
111	      // 1. Stretched-link overlay — see docblock point 1. Deliberately no z-index of its own
112	      // (stays at the default/auto stacking layer), so every control lifted in point 2 below
113	      // reliably paints above it regardless of DOM order.
114	      '[data-card-slot="content"] a::after': {
115	        content: '""',
116	        position: 'absolute',
117	        inset: 0,
118	      },
119	
120	      // 2. Every genuinely-interactive control sits above the stretched overlay. A plain `button`
121	      // type-selector under the relevant data-card-slot root reaches every control uniformly —
122	      // none of them declare their own data-card-slot, and none needs one: Content's bag button,
123	      // its notify-me button, and every ZimmSizeChip button nested inside its own sizeChips
124	      // wrapper are all real <button> descendants of [data-card-slot="content"].
125	      // Fix 1 (Scorer rework round 1): NO position value here. ZimmProductCardMedia's own
126	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
127	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
128	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
129	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
130	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
131	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
132	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
133	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
134	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
135	      '[data-card-slot="close"]': {
136	        zIndex: 1,
137	      },
138	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
139	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
140	      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
141	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
142	      '[data-card-slot="carousel"]': {
143	        zIndex: 1,
144	      },
145	      '[data-card-slot="content"] button': {
146	        position: 'relative',
147	        zIndex: 1,
148	      },
149	
150	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
151	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
152	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
153	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
154	      ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
155	        // Home: price starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
156	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
157	      }),
158	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
159	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
160	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'none' },
161	      }),
162	
163	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
164	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
165	          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
166	          '&:hover [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'block' },
167	          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
168	          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
169	          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. `:focus-within` on this same
170	          // root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that focus landing
171	          // on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers the reveal —
172	          // mirrors zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own `_focusWithin` sibling
173	          // to `_hover`. Expressed as a separate string key (not a comma-joined
174	          // `'&:hover, &:focus-within ...'` selector) to match that same established idiom;
175	          // this file already uses raw selector strings rather than Chakra's `_hover`/
176	          // `_focusWithin` shorthand props because the descendant-combinator path has to be
177	          // baked into the selector itself.
178	          '&:focus-within [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'block' },
179	        }),
180	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
181	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
182	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it.
183	          '&:hover [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
184	          // Fix 2 — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale. Keyboard focus
185	          // anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector exactly as hover
186	          // does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a different partial
187	          // one.
188	          '&:focus-within [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
189	        }),
190	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
191	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it.
192	          '&:hover [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'block' },
193	          // Fix 2 — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
194	          '&:focus-within [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'block' },
195	        }),
196	      },
197	    },
198	  }),
199	};

40	 * own by itself:

43	 *      in the whole composed tree. Its `::after` is stretched to `inset: 0` against THIS
44	 *      component's own `root` — the nearest positioned ancestor. Confirmed by reading
45	 *      `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` directly: neither its `root` nor `nameRow`, `nameLink`, or
46	 *      any other part sets `position` anywhere in that file, so nothing between the `<a>` and
47	 *      this `root` intercepts the containing-block chain. (`ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `root`
48	 *      IS `position: relative`, but Media is a *sibling* of Content under this organism's root,

51	 *      overlay's own (left unset), or the invisible overlay would intercept their clicks first.
52	 *      Three separate, single-selector keys rather than one comma-joined selector: verified via
53	 *      this project's own installed Stylis (v4.2.0 — the same engine Emotion/Chakra invoke at
54	 *      runtime, confirmed by direct compilation) that a comma-separated list DOES distribute this
55	 *      recipe's generated class across every branch correctly, but three plain keys need no such
56	 *      verification to trust at a glance and are each individually addressable from a test. Only
57	 *      ONE of the three (`content` buttons) also adds `position: relative` — that element is
58	 *      `position: static` by default in its own component recipe, so a positioned ancestor is
59	 *      needed for z-index to apply at all. `close` and `carousel` are the two exceptions:
60	 *      `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own recipe already positions each of them directly (`close` via
61	 *      `position: absolute, top: 0, right: 0`; `carousel` via `position: absolute, top: 50%, ...`),
62	 *      so each needs (and gets) only the z-index bump here:
63	 *        - `close` — a competing `position` value previously declared alongside it had HIGHER
64	 *          specificity than Media's own rule (this rule is a class+attribute descendant selector;
65	 *          Media's is a single class) and silently won the cascade, knocking the remove button out
66	 *          of its pinned top-right corner into normal document flow (Fix 1). See the inline
67	 *          comment at that key below and index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe block for the proof.
68	 *        - `carousel` — Fix 3 (found during the manual real-browser check performed after the

77	 *          regardless of its `position`/`z-index`. That traps each arrow button's `zIndex: 1`
78	 *          *inside* the carousel wrapper's own stacking context — it only wins ordering battles

80	 *          content overlay), because the whole `carousel` box is itself just an ordinary
81	 *          z-index:auto participant one level up — and, being earlier in DOM order than
82	 *          `[data-card-slot="content"]`, it lost. Moving the lift to the `carousel` WRAPPER itself
83	 *          (already `position: absolute` from Media's own recipe, so only `zIndex: 1` is needed
84	 *          here, same as `close`) fixes this: the wrapper's own stacking context — not one buried
85	 *          inside it — is what gets compared against the overlay, and it wins outright, carrying
86	 *          both arrow buttons above the overlay with it. This is exactly the gap
87	 *          index.test.tsx's own "KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock warns about — jsdom resolves no
88	 *          stacking contexts at all, so this shipped past every automated check and was only
89	 *          found by a real click in a real browser. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 3" describe block.

91	 *      hidden-by-default price), gated by the same `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` query
92	 *      `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` already uses for its own arrows/indicator split. Each reveal
93	 *      rule fires on `:hover` OR `:focus-within` on this same root (Fix 2 rework below) — `:hover`
94	 *      alone would leave every reveal permanently unreachable by keyboard on a hover-capable
95	 *      device, since `display: none` removes the unconditional-state element from the tab order

108	 *          hover; every Mobile Unavailable reference (Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so
109	 *          whatever it shows is the only state a touch pointer ever sees) shows it plainly with no

138	      width: '100%',

165	        zIndex: 1,
166	      },
167	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See

171	      '[data-card-slot="carousel"]': {

173	      },

All three findings are fixed, tested (including deliberate falsification), and re-verified live against the real Figma references — no regressions on Home/PLP/Wishlist's normal hover behavior. Here's where Step 6 stands now:

**Real-browser interaction matrix — complete:**
- Bag button ✅, close/remove button ✅ (pinned + clickable), stretched-link click-through ✅ (verified via `document.activeElement`, not just callback wiring), hover-reveal ✅, focus-within reveal+revert ✅, and the carousel arrows ✅ — the last one only after finding and fixing a genuine stacking-context bug: the arrow-lift rule targeted the buttons individually, but Media's own `transform: translateY(-50%)` on the carousel wrapper trapped their z-index in its own stacking context, so the stretched-link overlay was silently winning every real click despite every jsdom test passing. Fixed by lifting the wrapper itself instead.

**Visual audit against live Figma (this pass), all fixed:**
- **A** — size chips rendered pixel-flush (0 gap) instead of `justify-content: space-between` across the full card width.
- **B** — the Wishlist story never populated size-chip data, so its hover state showed an empty gap instead of the real chip row.
- **C** — unavailable items were getting the full price→size-chip hover swap (wrong — nothing to pick when out of stock) and "Notify me" was rendering unconditionally instead of hover-gated on desktop / always-visible on touch. Fixed in two passes — the first fix suppressed the swap but left size chips falling back to their visible default, caught by re-checking the live render against Figma before calling it done.

Every fix has a passing test, and I deliberately broke each new assertion once to confirm it actually fails without the fix. `tsc`, lint, and the full touched-suite (119 tests) are all clean.

One thing still needs your call before I can commit: the **mobile bag-icon visibility gap** flagged earlier (Figma hides the bag icon on mobile PLP/PDP; today's build shows it on every breakpoint) — fixing it needs a new `data-card-slot="bag"` attribute added to the already-committed `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx`, which is outside this step's file scope without your sign-off.

11	 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
12	 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
13	 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
14	 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
15	 *
16	 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
17	 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; hover reveals price; arrows appear
18	 *             (Media's own concern, driven purely by image count, not variation).
19	 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
20	 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
21	 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
22	 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
23	 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
24	 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
25	 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
26	 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
27	 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover), but the
28	 *             design is the source of truth here per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule.
29	 *
30	 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
31	 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
32	 *
33	 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
34	 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
35	 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
36	 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
37	 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
38	 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
39	 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
40	 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
41	 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
42	 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
43	 *     hover/focus-within, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
44	 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
45	 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
46	 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
47	 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
48	 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';

/**
 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
 *
 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; hover reveals price; arrows appear
 *             (Media's own concern, driven purely by image count, not variation).
 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover), but the
 *             design is the source of truth here per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-within, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.

Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
