195	      // `close` recipe part already sets `position: 'absolute', top: 0, right: 0` on this exact
196	      // element (that's how the remove button pins to the image's top-right corner). This rule's
197	      // `.css-root [data-card-slot="close"]` descendant+attribute selector has HIGHER
198	      // specificity than Media's own single-class rule, so a competing `position` value declared
199	      // here would win the cascade and knock the button out of its pinned position into normal
200	      // flow — which is exactly what shipped here before this fix. The element is already
201	      // positioned (by Media's own recipe), which is all `zIndex` needs to take effect; no
202	      // `position` re-declaration was ever necessary. See index.test.tsx's "Fix 1" describe
203	      // blocks for the object-shape and real-DOM/getComputedStyle proof.
204	      '[data-card-slot="close"]': {
205	        zIndex: 1,
206	      },
207	      // Fix 3 — zIndex only, on the carousel WRAPPER, not on each arrow `button` inside it. See
208	      // docblock point 2 above for why lifting the buttons individually left them unclickable in
209	      // a real browser (a `transform`-induced stacking context on this wrapper trapped their own
210	      // zIndex) despite passing every jsdom test.
211	      '[data-card-slot="carousel"]': {
212	        zIndex: 1,
213	      },
214	      '[data-card-slot="content"] button': {
215	        position: 'relative',
216	        zIndex: 1,
217	      },
218	
219	      // 3. Hover-reveal swap — see docblock point 3. The unconditional (outside-media-query)
220	      // half of each flag below is what makes a touch/no-hover pointer see the *default* state
221	      // permanently: it never matches HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all, so whichever rule fired outside
222	      // it (or the total absence of one) is the only state that pointer type ever sees.
223	      ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
224	        // Home: price starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
225	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
226	      }),
227	      ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
228	        // PLP/Wishlist: size-selector starts hidden at every breakpoint/pointer type...
229	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'none' },
230	      }),
231	      // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Unconditional and permanent, on every device: an
232	      // out-of-stock item never gets the size-selector, in any state, so this is the only rule
233	      // for it at all when `sizeSelectorUnavailable` is true (no corresponding reveal exists
234	      // anywhere, inside or outside the media query below).
235	      ...(sizeSelectorUnavailable && {
236	        '[data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'none' },
237	      }),
238	
239	      [HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]: {
240	        ...(hoverRevealsPrice && {
241	          // ...and is only revealed here, once a hover-capable pointer actually hovers the card.
242	          '&:hover [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'block' },
243	          // Fix 2 (Scorer rework round 1): `display: none` removes an element from the tab
244	          // order entirely, so a keyboard-only user on a hover-capable device (tabbing, not
245	          // hovering) could never reveal this via `:hover` alone. `:focus-within` on this same
246	          // root — scoped here, not on the price/size-chip wrapper itself, so that focus landing
247	          // on ANY descendant control (name link, bag button, size chip) triggers the reveal —
248	          // mirrors zimmSearchInput.css.ts's container/zimmFormRow's own `_focusWithin` sibling
249	          // to `_hover`. Expressed as a separate string key (not a comma-joined
250	          // `'&:hover, &:focus-within ...'` selector) to match that same established idiom;
251	          // this file already uses raw selector strings rather than Chakra's `_hover`/
252	          // `_focusWithin` shorthand props because the descendant-combinator path has to be
253	          // baked into the selector itself.
254	          '&:focus-within [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'block' },
255	        }),
256	        ...(hoverHidesPrice && {
257	          // PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default (no unconditional rule needed above) and
258	          // hides only here, in favour of the size-selector reveal alongside it.
259	          '&:hover [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
260	          // Fix 2 — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale. Keyboard focus
261	          // anywhere in the card must hide price in favour of the size-selector exactly as hover
262	          // does, so a keyboard user sees the identical revealed state, not a different partial
263	          // one.
264	          '&:focus-within [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="price"]': { display: 'none' },
265	        }),
266	        ...(hoverRevealsSizeSelector && {
267	          // ...and is only revealed here, matching the price swap alongside it.
268	          '&:hover [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'block' },
269	          // Fix 2 — see the hoverRevealsPrice block above for the full rationale.
270	          '&:focus-within [data-card-slot="content"] [data-card-slot="sizeChips"]': { display: 'block' },
271	        }),
272	        // Fix C — see docblock point 4. Both the "hidden by default" declaration AND its reveal

content.text:
Full sweep against all 21 nodes is done, with one important twist: while verifying Findings E/F/G live, I caught a real bug in my *own* just-shipped Fix D/F code — not a new Figma misalignment.

**Findings E, F, G — all fixed and verified:**
- **E**: Home's price was hidden unconditionally, so it never appeared on mobile at all (no Hover variant exists there to reveal it). Now scoped inside the hover-capable media query only, matching notify-me's existing pattern. Confirmed live: Home now shows price on mobile.
- **F**: PLP/Wishlist now hide price on mobile specifically when unavailable (swapped for "Notify me"), instead of showing both together as the old desktop-only logic did everywhere. Confirmed live.
- **G**: Wishlist's bag icon now hides on mobile only when unavailable (PLP's own mobile hide stays unconditional). Added the missing `WishlistOutOfStock` story to demonstrate it. Confirmed live, both states.

**The twist**: implementing E/F/G revealed that Fix D and Fix F each independently added a `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` object key to the same style object — a plain object spread doesn't deep-merge two spreads sharing a key, so whichever came later silently wiped out the other's entirely. This shipped past every jsdom test because none of them exercised both flags at once — exactly the combination a real unavailable PLP card produces. Caught it by re-checking the actual live render against Figma rather than trusting green tests, confirmed the root cause via `document.styleSheets`, and fixed it by merging both into one shared `[DESKTOP_QUERY]` block (mirroring how `[HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY]` was already correctly structured). Added a regression test that renders the realistic combined-flags case, deliberately reintroduced the collision to confirm the test catches it, then restored the fix.

Final state: `tsc`, lint, and `audit:tokens` all clean; 134 tests passing across the 6 touched suites, including falsification of every new assertion. The two Hero/`Defualt` nodes remain confirmed out of scope, nothing new there.

Step 6 is ready to commit whenever you give the word.

content.text:
Good catch — let me give you the precise breakdown rather than a hand-wave.

**Hover and Mobile/Desktop aren't separate stories by design, not by oversight.** In this codebase's convention (and Storybook's generally), a story is one set of props; hover is a pointer pseudo-state and viewport width is a responsive concern — both are checked by interacting with *the same* story, not by duplicating it. That's why every story here says "Hover to check X" in its docblock, and it's exactly how I tested mobile behavior all session (`resize_window` on the existing story, never a separate "Mobile" story). That convention collapses your 20 nodes like this:

- Desktop: 3 types × Default/Hover × available/unavailable = 12 → collapses to 6 (hover isn't a story)
- Mobile: 3 types × available/unavailable (no Hover variant exists) = 6 → collapses into the *same* 6 (viewport isn't a story either)
- Hero/`Defualt` ×2 → confirmed out of scope, no AC

So the honest target is **6 meaningful prop-combinations**, each checked across both states by hand. Against that:

| Combination | Story | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Home, available | `Home` | ✅ |
| Home, **unavailable** | — | ❌ **missing** |
| PLP, available | `PLP` (and `Default`, which is an exact duplicate of it) | ✅ (redundant pair) |
| PLP, unavailable | `PLPOutOfStock` | ✅ |
| Wishlist, available | `Wishlist` | ✅ |
| Wishlist, unavailable | `WishlistOutOfStock` | ✅ (just added) |

Plus `SingleImage`/`MultipleImages`, which demonstrate Media's image-count behavior rather than a new variation.

So the real answer: there's a genuine gap — **no `HomeOutOfStock` story** — and it's inconsistent that I caught it for Wishlist (Fix G) but not for Home, especially since Finding E/F directly changed Home's unavailable-on-mobile behavior this session. There's also a small redundancy (`Default` and `PLP` are byte-identical args). Want me to add `HomeOutOfStock` and drop the `Default`/`PLP` duplication?

38	      // dist `require()`s the CJS file while a raw `import` (used by a Storybook story
39	      // authored under overrides/) resolves the ESM file — two distinct files, so two
40	      // distinct copies of QueryClientProvider's module-scope Context objects. A
41	      // QueryClientProvider rendered from one copy is invisible to useQueryClient() called
42	      // from the other, throwing "No QueryClient set" despite a provider clearly being an
